title: Tell the verifier records/ and private paths are absent by design
summary: Review note n3: the verifier prompt and brief should say, as the producer and reader prompts do, that records/, owner-private files, and history are absent from its snapshot by design, so it neither hunts for them nor reports their absence as a finding. The audience is the verifier model and maintainers reading its findings.

defaults_applied.how: New unit test plus workspace test and clippy criteria.
Limited to verifier prompt, brief, changelog.
Test asserts the brief output contains the statement.
Wording is plain for outside readers.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The existing line 12 of verifier.md already says the snapshot lacks records/ but not that this is by design nor that absence is not a finding; the edit extends it.
The brief gets a short sentence in verifier_brief, e.g. in the Scope or change section, mirroring the producer brief wording.
CHANGELOG.md has entries for prompt changes, so one is added.

acceptance_criteria.text: crates/athena-context/prompts/verifier.md states that records/, the owner's private files, and history are absent from the snapshot by design, that the verifier should not search for them, and that their absence is not itself a finding.

verifier_brief in crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs emits a sentence that records/, private files, and history are absent by design and not a finding; producer and reader briefs/prompts are unchanged.
A new unit test in briefs.rs asserts verifier_brief output contains the 'absent by design' statement naming records/ and private files; run `cargo test -p athena-context` and see it pass.
`cargo test --workspace`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets`, and `cargo fmt --check` all pass, including tests pinning prompt text.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry for the verifier prompt/brief change, and no other files change.

out_of_scope: Changing producer or reader prompts and briefs
Changing how the verifier snapshot is built
departures: Small mechanical change, so cost and time are somewhat below the reference.
